claims: A Certified Public Accountant (CPA) is a licensed accounting professional.
A CPA has passed the Uniform CPA Exam.
A CPA has met state education requirements typically of 150 credit hours.
A CPA has completed professional experience.
CPAs earn, on average, over $82,000 annually.
CPAs often earn 10-15% more than non-certified accountants.
CPAs perform auditing.
CPAs perform tax preparation.
CPAs perform financial consulting.
CPA education requires a bachelor’s degree in accounting or a related field.
CPA education typically requires 150 semester hours of education.
150 semester hours of education is 30 more than a standard 4-year degree.
The Uniform CPA Examination has three 4-hour core sections.
The Uniform CPA Examination has one discipline section.
CPA requires work experience in accounting.
CPA experience requirements vary by state.
CPA work experience is usually supervised by a licensed CPA.
It generally takes 5–6 years to meet the requirements to become a CPA.
A bachelor's degree takes 4 years.
The 150-hour requirement is often met by obtaining a Master's degree.
CPAs prepare and review financial statements.
CPAs file tax returns.
CPAs provide tax planning strategies.
CPAs audit financial records for regulatory compliance.
CPAs offer management consulting and advisory services.
